- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.4) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.4), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to reflect risk aversion or market panic.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike in forecast (e.g., >10% from prior), true outcome often lags or reverses; apply 2–5 day lag correction or cap peak at 1.5x prior high.  
- If forecast mean is significantly below true mean (e.g., >5% gap), model underestimates trend; add 0.5–1.0x sentiment-weighted adjustment to mean.  
- If sentiment is volatile or mixed (±0.3), model often overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast with 3-day moving average or reduce volatility by 20%.  
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently misses late-period momentum; add 1–2% upward bias if sentiment turns positive in last 5 days.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65), model often overreacts; reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until reversion.
